DESCRIPTION:

commonly has: (a) pausing doesn't actually stop the clock (timer
keeps ticking in the background), or (b) resuming resets to the
full duration instead of continuing from the paused value. Neither
has been explicitly covered by the existing tests — reset-during-
phase tests only check RESET, not pause.
NAME: Pause freezes the countdown; resume continues from where it left off

DESCRIPTION:
Measures actual behavior rather than asserting a guessed
expectation. A prior version hard-coded `expected_after =
remaining_before - 5`, assuming the countdown continues on a
wall-clock basis while backgrounded — but a live run showed the
countdown dropping only ~1s across ~5+ real seconds backgrounded,
which is the OPPOSITE of round-trip measurement noise (noise would
make elapsed time look bigger, not smaller). That's a real signal:
the countdown likely pauses (or nearly freezes) while backgrounded.

Whether that's correct depends on product intent — a meditation
app pausing your session when you leave is a defensible design
choice, not obviously a bug. This test measures real elapsed wall
time precisely and reports both the "paused" and "kept ticking"
hypotheses; it only fails on genuinely unambiguous problems
(time going backwards/increasing, or a session that silently
resets to READY instead of resuming in some state).

DESCRIPTION:
CONFIRMED (2026-08-08, live Inspector sequence on Coherent
Breathing): the counter's "current" directly matches the active
phase's 1-indexed position in the cycle — READY shows the "—"
placeholder, INHALE (phase 1 of 2) shows "1/2 PHASE", EXHALE
(phase 2 of 2) shows "2/2 PHASE". No off-by-one: current reflects
the phase that's ACTIVE RIGHT NOW, not the one about to start.

This asserts the exact expected value at each phase (current ==
that phase's position in the pattern), not just "increments
consistently" — the earlier version hedged on which convention
was in use; that's no longer necessary now it's been observed
directly.

DESCRIPTION:
UI state machines are a common source of double-tap bugs (e.g.
both taps registering as "start", leaving two competing timers).
This doesn't assert a specific end state (start-then-pause could
legitimately land as either playing or paused depending on how
fast the taps land) — it asserts the app doesn't end up in a
broken state: phase label must be one of the four known values,
and the countdown must still be readable without raising.
NAME: Rapid double-tap on play/pause does not corrupt session state
